## Scope of this Part

## 36.1

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.1] (1)  This Part contains a self-contained procedural code about offers to settle made pursuant to the procedure set out in this Part (“Part 36 offers”). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.1] (2) Section I of this Part contains general rules about Part 36 offers. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.1] (3) Section II of this Part contains rules about Part 36 offers where a claim is one to which Section VI (fixed costs in the fast track), Section VII (fixed costs in the intermediate track) or Section VIII (claims for noise-induced hearing loss) of Part 45 applies. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.1] (4) Section III of this Part contains rules about offers to settle where the parties have followed the Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents (“the RTA Protocol”) or the Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims (“the EL/PL Protocol”) and have started proceedings under Part 8 in accordance with Practice Direction 49F. ## I PART 36 OFFERS TO SETTLE

## General

## Scope of this Section

## 36.2

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.2] (1) This Section—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.2] (a)applies to an offer to settle to which Section II of this Part applies, unless otherwise stated; but

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.2] (b)does not apply to an offer to settle to which Section III applies. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.2] (2) Nothing in this Section prevents a party making an offer to settle in whatever way that party chooses, but if the offer is not made in accordance with rule 36.5, it will not have the consequences specified in this Section. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.2] (Rule 44.2 requires the court to consider an offer to settle that does not have the costs consequences set out in this Section in deciding what order to make about costs.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.2] (3) A Part 36 offer may be made in respect of the whole, or part of, or any issue that arises in—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.2] (a) a claim, counterclaim or other additional claim; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.2] (b) an appeal or cross-appeal from a decision made at a trial. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.2] (Rules 20.2 and 20.3 provide that counterclaims and other additional claims are treated as claims and that references to a claimant or a defendant include a party bringing or defending an additional claim.)

## Definitions

## 36.3 In this Section—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.3 In this Section—] (a) the party who makes an offer is the “offeror”;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.3 In this Section—] (b) the party to whom an offer is made is the “offeree”;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.3 In this Section—] (c) a “trial” means any trial in a case whether it is a trial of all issues or a trial of liability, quantum or some other issue in the case;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.3 In this Section—] (d) a trial is “in progress” from the time when it starts until the time when judgment is given or handed down;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.3 In this Section—] (e) a case is “decided” when all issues in the case have been determined, whether at one or more trials;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.3 In this Section—] (f) “trial judge” includes the judge (if any) allocated in advance to conduct a trial; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.3 In this Section—] (g) “the relevant period” means—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.3 In this Section—] (i) in the case of an offer made not less than 21 days before a trial, the period specified under rule 36.5(1)(c) or such longer period as the parties agree;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.3 In this Section—] (ii) otherwise, the period up to the end of such trial. ## Application of Part 36 to appeals

## 36.4

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.4] (1) Except where a Part 36 offer is made in appeal proceedings, it shall have the consequences set out in this Section only in relation to the costs of the proceedings in respect of which it is made, and not in relation to the costs of any appeal from a decision in those proceedings. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.4] (2) Where a Part 36 offer is made in appeal proceedings, references in this Section to a term in the first column below shall be treated, unless the context requires otherwise, as references to the corresponding term in the second column—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.4] Term | Corresponding term

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.4] Claim | Appeal

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.4] Counterclaim | Cross-appeal

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.4] Case | Appeal proceedings

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.4] Claimant | Appellant

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.4] Defendant | Respondent

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.4] Trial | Appeal hearing

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.4] Trial judge | Appeal judge

## Making offers

## Form and content of a Part 36 offer

## 36.5

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (1) A Part 36 offer must—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (a) be in writing;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (b) make clear that it is made pursuant to Part 36;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (c) specify a period of not less than 21 days within which the defendant will be liable for the claimant’s costs in accordance with rule 36.13 or 36.23 if the offer is accepted;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (d) state whether it relates to the whole of the claim or to part of it or to an issue that arises in it and if so to which part or issue; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (e) state whether it takes into account any counterclaim. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (Rule 36.7 makes provision for when a Part 36 offer is made.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (2) Paragraph (1)(c) does not apply if the offer is made less than 21 days before the start of a trial. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (3) In appropriate cases, a Part 36 offer must contain such further information as is required by rule 36.18 (personal injury claims for future pecuniary loss), rule 36.19 (offer to settle a claim for provisional damages), and rule 36.20 (deduction of benefits). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (4) A Part 36 offer which offers to pay or offers to accept a sum of money will be treated as inclusive of all interest until—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (a) the date on which the period specified under rule 36.5(1)(c) expires; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (b) if rule 36.5(2) applies, a date 21 days after the date the offer was made. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.5] (5) A Part 36 offer to accept a sum of money may make provision for accrual of interest on such sum after the date specified in paragraph (4). If such an offer does not make any such provision, it shall be treated as inclusive of all interest up to the date of acceptance if it is later accepted. ## Part 36 offers – defendant’s offer

## 36.6

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.6] (1) Subject to rules 36.18(3) and 36.19(1), a Part 36 offer by a defendant to pay a sum of money in settlement of a claim must be an offer to pay a single sum of money. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.6] (2) A defendant’s offer that includes an offer to pay all or part of the sum at a date later than 14 days following the date of acceptance will not be treated as a Part 36 offer unless the offeree accepts the offer. ## Time when a Part 36 offer is made

## 36.7

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.7] (1) A Part 36 offer may be made at any time, including before the commencement of proceedings. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.7] (2) A Part 36 offer is made when it is served on the offeree. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.7] (Part 6 provides detailed rules about service of documents.)

## Clarifying, withdrawing and changing the terms of offers

## Clarification of a Part 36 offer

## 36.8

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.8] (1) The offeree may, within 7 days of a Part 36 offer being made, request the offeror to clarify the offer. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.8] (2) If the offeror does not give the clarification requested under paragraph (1) within 7 days of receiving the request, the offeree may, unless the trial has started, apply for an order that the offeror do so. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.8] (Part 23 contains provisions about making an application to the court.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.8] (3) If the court makes an order under paragraph (2), it must specify the date when the Part 36 offer is to be treated as having been made. ## Withdrawing or changing the terms of a Part 36 offer generally

## 36.9

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (1) A Part 36 offer can only be withdrawn, or its terms changed, if the offeree has not previously served notice of acceptance. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (2) The offeror withdraws the offer or changes its terms by serving written notice of the withdrawal or change of terms on the offeree. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (Rule 36.17(7) deals with the costs consequences following judgment of an offer which is withdrawn.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (3) Subject to rule 36.10, such notice of withdrawal or change of terms takes effect when it is served on the offeree. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (Rule 36.10 makes provision about when permission is required to withdraw or change the terms of an offer before the expiry of the relevant period.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (4) Subject to paragraph (1), after expiry of the relevant period—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (a) the offeror may withdraw the offer or change its terms without the permission of the court; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (b) the offer may be automatically withdrawn in accordance with its terms. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (5) Where the offeror changes the terms of a Part 36 offer to make it more advantageous to the offeree—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (a) such improved offer shall be treated, not as the withdrawal of the original offer; but as the making of a new Part 36 offer on the improved terms; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.9] (b) subject to rule 36.5(2), the period specified under rule 36.5(1)(c) shall be 21 days or such longer period (if any) identified in the written notice referred to in paragraph (2). ## Withdrawing or changing the terms of a Part 36 offer before the expiry of the relevant period

## 36.10

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.10] (1) Subject to rule 36.9(1), this rule applies where the offeror serves notice before expiry of the relevant period of withdrawal of the offer or change of its terms to be less advantageous to the offeree. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.10] (2) Where this rule applies—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.10] (a) if the offeree has not served notice of acceptance of the original offer by the expiry of the relevant period, the offeror’s notice has effect on the expiry of that period; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.10] (b) if the offeree serves notice of acceptance of the original offer before the expiry of the relevant period, that acceptance has effect unless the offeror applies to the court for permission to withdraw the offer or to change its terms—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.10] (i) within 7 days of the offeree’s notice of acceptance; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.10] (ii) if earlier, before the first day of trial. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.10] (3) On an application under paragraph (2)(b), the court may give permission for the original offer to be withdrawn or its terms changed if satisfied that there has been a change of circumstances since the making of the original offer and that it is in the interests of justice to give permission. ## Accepting offers

## Acceptance of a Part 36 offer

## 36.11

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (1) A Part 36 offer is accepted by serving written notice of acceptance on the offeror. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (2) Subject to paragraphs (3) and (4) and to rule 36.12, a Part 36 offer may be accepted at any time (whether or not the offeree has subsequently made a different offer), unless it has already been withdrawn. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (Rule 21.10 deals with compromise, etc. by or on behalf of a child or protected party.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (Rules 36.9 and 36.10 deal with withdrawal of Part 36 offers.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (3) The court’s permission is required to accept a Part 36 offer where—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (a) rule 36.15(4) applies;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (b) rule 36.20(3)(b) applies, the relevant period has expired and further deductible amounts have been paid to the claimant since the date of the offer;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (c) an apportionment is required under rule 41.3A; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (d) a trial is in progress. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (Rule 36.15 deals with offers by some but not all of multiple defendants.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (Rule 36.20 defines “deductible amounts”.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (Rule 41.3A requires an apportionment in proceedings under the Fatal Accidents Act 1976 1 and Law Reform (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1934 2 .)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.11] (4) Where the court gives permission under paragraph (3), unless all the parties have agreed costs, the court must make an order dealing with costs, and may order that the costs consequences set out in rule 36.13 apply. ## Acceptance of a Part 36 offer in a split-trial case

## 36.12

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.12] (1) This rule applies in any case where there has been a trial but the case has not been decided within the meaning of rule 36.3. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.12] (2) Any Part 36 offer which relates only to parts of the claim or issues that have already been decided can no longer be accepted. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.12] (3) Subject to paragraph (2) and unless the parties agree, any other Part 36 offer cannot be accepted earlier than 7 clear days after judgment is given or handed down in such trial. ## Costs consequences of acceptance of a Part 36 offer

## 36.13

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (1) Subject to paragraphs (2) and (4) and to rule 36.23, where a Part 36 offer is accepted within the relevant period the claimant will be entitled to the costs of the proceedings (including their recoverable pre-action costs) up to the date on which notice of acceptance was served on the offeror. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (Rule 36.20 makes provision for the costs consequences of accepting a Part 36 offer in certain personal injury claims where the claim no longer proceeds under the RTA or EL/PL Protocol.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (2) Where—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (a) a defendant’s Part 36 offer relates to part only of the claim; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (b) at the time of serving notice of acceptance within the relevant period the claimant abandons the balance of the claim,

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] the claimant will only be entitled to the costs of such part of the claim unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (3) Except where the recoverable costs are fixed by these Rules, costs under paragraphs (1) and (2) are to be assessed on the standard basis if the amount of costs is not agreed. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (Rule 44.3(2) explains the standard basis for the assessment of costs.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (Rule 44.9 contains provisions about when a costs order is deemed to have been made and applying for an order under section 194(3) of the Legal Services Act 2007 3 .)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (Part 45 provides for fixed costs in certain classes of case.)

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (4) Where—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (a) a Part 36 offer which was made less than 21 days before the start of a trial is accepted; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (b) a Part 36 offer which relates to the whole of the claim is accepted after expiry of the relevant period; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (c) subject to paragraph (2), a Part 36 offer which does not relate to the whole of the claim is accepted at any time,

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] the liability for costs must be determined by the court unless the parties have agreed the costs. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (5) Where paragraph (4)(b) applies but the parties cannot agree the liability for costs, the court must, unless it considers it unjust to do so, order that—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (a) the claimant be awarded costs up to the date on which the relevant period expired; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (b) the offeree do pay the offeror’s costs for the period from the date of expiry of the relevant period to the date of acceptance. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (6) In considering whether it would be unjust to make the orders specified in paragraph (5), the court must take into account all the circumstances of the case including the matters listed in rule 36.17(5). [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.13] (7) The claimant’s costs include any costs incurred in dealing with the defendant’s counterclaim if the Part 36 offer states that it takes it into account. ## Other effects of acceptance of a Part 36 offer

## 36.14

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (1) If a Part 36 offer is accepted, the claim will be stayed. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (2) In the case of acceptance of a Part 36 offer which relates to the whole claim, the stay will be upon the terms of the offer. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (3) If a Part 36 offer which relates to part only of the claim is accepted, the claim will be stayed as to that part upon the terms of the offer. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (4) If the approval of the court is required before a settlement can be binding, any stay which would otherwise arise on the acceptance of a Part 36 offer will take effect only when that approval has been given. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (5) Any stay arising under this rule will not affect the power of the court—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (a) to enforce the terms of a Part 36 offer; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (b) to deal with any question of costs (including interest on costs) relating to the proceedings. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (6) Unless the parties agree otherwise in writing, where a Part 36 offer that is or includes an offer to pay or accept a single sum of money is accepted, that sum must be paid to the claimant within 14 days of the date of—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (a) acceptance; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (b) the order when the court makes an order under rule 41.2 (order for an award of provisional damages) or rule 41.8 (order for an award of periodical payments), unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (7) If such sum is not paid within 14 days of acceptance of the offer, or such other period as has been agreed, the claimant may enter judgment for the unpaid sum. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (8) Where—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (a) a Part 36 offer (or part of a Part 36 offer) which is not an offer to which paragraph (6) applies is accepted; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] (b) a party alleges that the other party has not honoured the terms of the offer,

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.14] that party may apply to enforce the terms of the offer without the need for a new claim. ## Acceptance of a Part 36 offer made by one or more, but not all, defendants

## 36.15

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.15] (1)  This rule applies where the claimant wishes to accept a Part 36 offer made by one or more, but not all, of a number of defendants. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.15] (2) If the defendants are sued jointly or in the alternative, the claimant may accept the offer if—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.15] (a) the claimant discontinues the claim against those defendants who have not made the offer; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.15] (b) those defendants give written consent to the acceptance of the offer. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.15] (3) If the claimant alleges that the defendants have a several liability (GL) to the claimant, the claimant may—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.15] (a) accept the offer; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.15] (b) continue with the claims against the other defendants if entitled to do so. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.15] (4) In all other cases the claimant must apply to the court for permission to accept the Part 36 offer. ## Unaccepted offers

## Restriction on disclosure of a Part 36 offer

## 36.16

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (1) A Part 36 offer will be treated as “without prejudice except as to costs”. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (2) The fact that a Part 36 offer has been made and the terms of such offer must not be communicated to the trial judge until the case has been decided. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (3) Paragraph (2) does not apply—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (a) where the defence of tender before claim has been raised;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (b) where the proceedings have been stayed under rule 36.14 following acceptance of a Part 36 offer;

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (c) where the offeror and the offeree agree in writing that it should not apply; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (d) where, although the case has not been decided—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (i) any part of, or issue in, the case has been decided; and

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (ii) the Part 36 offer relates only to parts or issues that have been decided. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (4) In a case to which paragraph (3)(d)(i) applies, the trial judge—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (a) may be told whether or not there are Part 36 offers other than those referred to in paragraph (3)(d)(ii); but

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.16] (b) must not be told the terms of any such other offers unless any of paragraphs (3)(a) to (c) applies. ## Costs consequences following judgment

## 36.17

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (1) Subject to rule 36.24, this rule applies where upon judgment being entered—

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (a) a claimant fails to obtain a judgment more advantageous than a defendant’s Part 36 offer; or

[PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (b) judgment against the defendant is at least as advantageous to the claimant as the proposals contained in a claimant’s Part 36 offer. [PART 36 – OFFERS TO SETTLE > 36.17] (2) For the purposes of paragraph (1), in relation to any money claim or money element of a claim, “more advantageous” means better in money terms by any amount, however small, and “at least as advantageous” shall be construed accordingly.
